title: People’s Mañanera August 7
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity’s Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available[here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Inflation Falls and the Popular Economy Strengthens  
** Annual inflation fell to 3.12% in July, its lowest level in recent times.
President Claudia Sheinbaum noted that this is good news and attributed the
result to the PACIC—the agreement to keep fuel prices stable—and measures
against speculation. “Without these agreements, inflation would at least be
double that,” she added.

**Mexico and Peru Restore Diplomatic Relations  
** The President announced the restoration of diplomatic relations with Peru
following the arrival in Mexico of Betssy Chávez, a former minister under
President Pedro Castillo, who was granted asylum by the Mexican government.
She reiterated her support for Castillo and explained that “regardless of the
political orientations of governments, it is important for Mexico to maintain
diplomatic relations with the world.”

**Ayotzinapa: Investigations to Uncover the Truth Are Moving Forward  
** Sheinbaum reported that the arrest of former Guerrero Governor Ángel
Aguirre is part of the Federal Attorney General’s (FGR) investigations into
the forced disappearance of the 43 Ayotzinapa students, and she has asked for
a press conference to report on the progress of the investigations as soon as
legally possible. The President reiterated that “the goal is to uncover the
truth, find the (missing) young people, and ensure that justice is served.”

**With the United States: Coordination, Yes; Subordination, No  
** Sheinbaum rejected former U.S. Ambassador Ken Salazar’s call to close the
case of the transfer of drug kingpin “El Mayo” to the United States and
reiterated that it must be clarified whether there was interference by U.S.
government agencies on Mexican soil. The President emphasized that the
relationship with the United States will continue to be based on respect for
sovereignty, trust, and collaboration.

**Energy Sovereignty with Environmental Responsibility  
** The President affirmed that reducing dependence on imported gas is a
question of sovereignty and explained that alternatives are being analyzed to
strengthen energy security through renewable energy, efficiency, and new
technologies. She reiterated that any decision will be made on the basis of
scientific evidence and with the least possible environmental impact.

**Audience Rights: More Rights, Not Censorship  
** Sheinbaum reiterated that the guidelines on audience rights are still under
consultation and do not include censorship or content review. “Censorship
would mean that, if the government doesn’t like something, it orders it to be
removed, but there is nothing like that in the guidelines,” she explained.

**México Canta: A Culture of Peace for Youth  
** México Canta brought together 16,289 participants from Mexico and the
United States. The President noted that the song competition is part of the
Program for Peace and Against Addictions. “What’s important is that all of
them serve as role models for other young people,” Sheinbaum explained. The
grand final will be held on September 13, and the winning group will open the
Independence Day celebration.
